documents.title: Stanford Hybrid & Remote Work Longitudinal Study (Nicholas Bloom)
documents.summary: Long-term randomized controlled trials and surveys across 16,000+ workers analyzing output, turnover, and innovation across in-person, hybrid, and fully remote cohorts.
documents.evidence: Fully remote workers demonstrated a 13% performance increase primarily driven by fewer sick days and quieter work environments. However, fully remote setups experienced an 18% reduction in patent collaboration and cross-departmental spontaneous innovation compared to in-office peers.
citations: Nicholas Bloom et al., Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research (SIEPR), 'Hybrid Work Is Good for Employees and Companies', Nature 2024

documents.title: Environmental and Commuter Economic Dividends
documents.summary: Impact of telecommuting on transport carbon footprints, urban congestion, and employee cost of living.
documents.evidence: Working from home 2–4 days per week reduces individual transport greenhouse gas emissions by up to 54%. The average commuter reclaims 54 minutes per day in commute time and saves an estimated $4,500 to $6,000 annually on fuel, transit, and professional wardrobe.
citations: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS), 'Climate Mitigation Potential of Teleworking', 2023

documents.title: Workplace Mentorship Erosion & Urban Economic Hollow-Out
documents.summary: Adverse effects on entry-level employee career onboarding and commercial real estate downtown ecosystems.
documents.evidence: Junior software engineers receiving in-person code reviews and informal proximity mentorship received 24% more promotional recommendations in their first 24 months than remote equivalents. Commercial vacancy rates exceeded 25% in major city centers, shrinking municipal tax bases for transit and schools.
citations: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Reports, 'The Power of Proximity: In-Person Interaction and Mentorship', 2023
